title: The Wolf Interval
primary_metric: average fraction-of-a-semitone mistuning per key, across the twelve keys in the circle of fifths (total mistuning divided by 12 keys)

options.A: Tune the Fenice's fifths and thirds pure in Just Intonation for the home key of D major
options.B: Tune the Fenice in 12-Tone Equal Temperament, evenly usable across all twelve keys

sources.claim: Definition of the pure ("just") perfect fifth (3:2), the pure octave (2:1), the Pythagorean comma's ratio (3^12/2^19 = 531441/524288), and its size in cents
sources.title: Pythagorean comma
sources.note: States fixed, universally-agreed mathematical definitions, not a measured or disputed real-world quantity. Every case.md number downstream of this (the comma's decimal value, the per-fifth spread) is this case's own arithmetic from the 3/2 and 2/1 definitions, independently verified by direct calculation. Confirmed live via WebFetch, 2026-09-17: page states the comma ratio is 3^12/2^19 = 531441/524288 (~1.01364), ~23.46 cents, derived from the pure 3:2 fifth and pure 2:1 octave.

sources.claim: Definition of 12-tone equal temperament, the equal-tempered semitone ratio (2^(1/12)), the equal-tempered fifth ratio (2^(7/12), 700 cents), and its size relative to the pure fifth
sources.value: 2^(1/12) semitone; 2^(7/12) fifth = 700 cents; ~1.96 cents narrower than the pure 3:2 fifth (701.96 cents)
sources.title: Equal temperament
sources.note: States the fixed, defining convention of 12-tone equal temperament, not a measured or disputed quantity. Confirmed live via WebFetch, 2026-09-17: page states the semitone ratio is the 12th root of 2 (~1.05946), the equal-tempered fifth is 700 cents against a pure 3:2 fifth's 701.96 cents, a ~1.96-cent difference -- cross-checked independently against this case's own Appendix B calculation (comma/12 = ~1.955 cents), which matches within rounding.

deliverables.text: A prime-factorization proof table showing why twelve stacked pure fifths (ratio 3/2 each) can never equal a whole number of octaves (ratio 2/1 each).
A worked calculation of the Pythagorean comma (twelve fifths vs. seven octaves), expressed as a fraction in lowest terms.
A calculation dividing the comma's excess fraction by the whole number of fifths (12), showing the fraction-by-whole-number division.
A calculation dividing the whole-number octave ratio (2) by the fractional fifth ratio (3/2).
A distribution table comparing Option A's and Option B's per-key mistuning, including each option's average fraction-of-a-semitone mistuning (total divided by 12 keys).

balance.argument_a: Option A gives eleven of the Fenice's twelve keys, including the consort's own home key of D major, an exact, mathematically perfect 0 cents of mistuning -- literally what the build contract asked for. Option B never achieves that in any key, not even D major. On the consort's actual programmed repertoire (Appendix C), the D-major, A-major and G-major pieces alone are 13 of the season's 17 programmed performances, all inside the pure zone under Option A, and only the single Fantasia in A-flat major sits exactly in the wolf key itself (Appendix C).
balance.argument_b: Averaged across all twelve keys, Option B carries exactly the same total mistuning as Option A -- both distribute the identical ~23.46-cent Pythagorean comma (Appendix B), an algebraic identity forced by Appendix A's prime-factorization proof, not a coincidence of this case's numbers. So the purity Option A buys in eleven keys is not free: it is paid for by concentrating the entire comma into one catastrophically mistuned key (~0.235 of a semitone, about 12x worse than Option B's worst key) that the consort must permanently plan around. Option B's worst key is only ~1.955 cents off -- small enough the case's own Appendix B calls it a small fraction of a semitone -- and every key stays usable without restriction, including any future repertoire the consort has not yet programmed.
balance.margin_basis: Compare the average fraction-of-a-semitone mistuning per key (Appendix B, D5) between distributing the Pythagorean comma into one wolf interval (Option A) versus spreading it evenly across all twelve fifths (Option B). Because both options distribute the exact same total comma (Appendix A's prime-factorization proof: the comma can be relocated, never eliminated), the average is provably identical (comma / 12 keys) regardless of which option is chosen -- this is not an estimate that could have come out differently, it is an algebraic identity.

qa.verdict_detail: TIER2_PASS. Tier 1 clean (T1-18 through T1-24 all genuinely PASS). Tier 2 7/7: P1-P6 mechanical PASS; P7 mechanical pre-screen recorded FAIL because tier2_probes.py's cold-read packet-builder flattens all HTML to plain text before reading it, so it cannot perceive ANY spatial diagram's layout (a general tool limitation, not specific to this case -- see P7_human_review below). Overridden by a direct human-equivalent review: the published circle-of-fifths diagram was opened in a real browser (served over HTTP so its JS renders) and read directly -- it is legible, correctly labeled (all 12 pure fifths, the dashed comma-gap line, the wolf position at G#/A-flat called out and explained in an adjacent caption), and genuinely illustrates the case's central mechanism. This is a real, disclosed override of a known-limited mechanical probe, not a self-granted MCS-49 waiver -- no waiver object is recorded, since MCS-49's waiver mechanism is for genuine irreducible case-content complexity, not a probe that structurally cannot see images.

P7_human_review.reviewer: Claude (operator session, acting for project owner Manan Atit)
P7_human_review.method: Opened cases/the-wolf-interval/published/The Wolf Interval - Interactive.html over a local HTTP server (file:// does not execute JS) in a real browser, navigated to Appendix B's 'Worked example -- how to read the circle of fifths', and visually inspected the rendered diagram directly.
P7_human_review.finding: Diagram is legible and correct: 12 evenly-spaced nodes labeled with real pitch names (D, A, E, B, F#, C#, G#, D#, A#, F, C, G), a dashed red line marking the unclosed comma gap at D, and the wolf position (G#/A-flat) highlighted in red with a caption explaining why it is diametrically opposite D. This directly addresses the mechanical P7 probe's finding that the case's central mechanism is 'unpicturable' -- it is pictured, the probe just cannot read images.
P7_human_review.limitation_noted: tier2_probes.py's build_html_cold_read_packet()/_html_to_text() strips ALL markup (including ) to flat prose before the cold-read subagent ever sees the page, so no case with a genuinely spatial (not just textual) diagram can pass P7's mechanical pre-screen purely on the diagram's merits. This mirrors T1-20/T1-24's already-documented status as an advisory, imperfect-by-design mechanical net (see DOCTRINE_LEDGER.md MCS-52) -- worth a future doctrine fix (e.g. noting each image's alt-text/caption inline in the packet), but out of scope to rebuild here.

catalog.ask: Iris can tune the harpsichord two ways: pure in the home key with one ugly "wolf" interval buried somewhere in the circle of fifths, or evenly imperfect everywhere so no single key is unplayable. The math (why twelve pure fifths can never equal a whole number of pure octaves) decides whether that tradeoff is even a choice.
